contribution: Developing empirical methods for estimating demand, market power and productivity in differentiated-product industries (structural empirical industrial organization)
rationale: This is an uncertain guess from my own knowledge, not a confident forecast. Recent prizes went to institutions and growth (2024) and innovation-driven growth (2025), so a shift to microeconomic empirical methods fits the committee's habit of rotating fields. The BLP and Olley-Pakes methods are standard tools in industrial organization, trade and antitrust. They are heavily cited, and empirical IO has not yet been honored, since Tirole's 2014 prize was mainly for theory. Strong alternatives include Ernst Fehr and Colin Camerer (social preferences and experimental economics), Richard Blundell (microeconometrics and labor supply), and Olivier Blanchard (macroeconomics).
